item.title: Kinda fun guy...
item.content:encoded:
Quite new to all this; stumbled across SCP about a year ago and am slowly chewing my way through.

A lot of what I would suggest has already been put forth by others. The idea is neat, but lacks certain concrete features to give it the "oomph" that some other SCPs carry. It might be better to actually drop some details, rather than leave things open-ended. I would definitely think a "goal" on the part of the fun guys would make things more coherent.

It's also worth noting that no number of humans, under whatever sort of compulsion, could ever excavate a cavern without tools.

My main issue is simply one of style. The writing is far outside the style seen in other SCPs; it lacks the clinical, precise, and curt tone that the best ones share. There were a couple of places where standard Foundation vocabulary would have been better.

It's a nifty idea. And it needs some polish. Maybe a fun guy party is the goal, a super-shroom thereby generated to…?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Hm. I definitely like the idea of this, but something about it feels… Off. Maybe unfinished. Two things that I feel like could have (/should have?) been expanded on:

Mentally, SCP-925 who have cooperated exhibit behaviors on par with high-functioning autism.

Which behaviors? "High-functioning" isn't a very accurate word, since the kinds of "symptoms" and "functioning levels" of autistic people can vary greatly, even day-to-day.

SCP-925 specimens appear to be true hermaphrodites.

Do they have human reproductive systems, then? If not, what kind?

Well, maybe I'm just being nitpicky. First time actually posting, and all that… No vote for now, but some invisible points for a cool idea.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
While I appreciated this not going in the direction of giant orgy (I don't know why, I just thought that's where the big pit was heading)—

the followers will search the nearby area for materials to use as fertilizer, then grow mushrooms in the cavern, eating as little as possible to stay alive

this just seems bizarre, and not in the good way. It's just super-impractical in the Darwinian sense. I like most anything that features fungi and absurdity, but this one is just a bit disjointed. The interview logs are bland and somewhat confusing. Also: high-functioning autism? Is that really the right simile?

item.title: (no title)

I agree with Roget; the tone is inconsistent. Also feels like a few things could use some elaboration. It grows mushrooms, but what kind of mushrooms? If it is mushrooms in general does it show a preference for a certain type of mushroom? It's a little too vague for me. Also noticed a few errors

SCP-925X-D-1: I feel pretty good, guy. You?

What's with the random X?

Specimens of SCP-925 are to be kept in individual standard 5 meter by 5 meter steel cells.

This cell only has two dimension.

Of course those last two things are nitpicks. Major issue was the tone.
